# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_028_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 28

**1** Jesus said: "I planted myself in the middle of the world, and I showed myself to them in the flesh.

**2** Every one of them was drunk. Not one of them was thirsty.

**3** My soul grieved for the human race — they are blind in their hearts. They don't see that they came into the world with nothing and will leave with nothing.

**4** Right now they're drunk. But when they sleep off their wine, they will change their minds."

---

**Translation Notes (PNEUMA):**
- "Planted myself" — the deliberate establishment in the world rendered as taking root
- "Not one of them" — the universality of the drunkenness emphasized
- "Grieved" — stronger than "ached"; the emotional weight of Jesus's response
- "Blind in their hearts" — the organ of inner vision specified
- "Came with nothing... leave with nothing" — the emptiness rendered as bare existence
- "Change their minds" — the literal meaning of *metanoeō* (to think again/differently)
